plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a high-index/low-index alternating dielectric stack (HfO2/MgF2) can achieve solar-blind UV bandpass filtering with visible/NIR suppression through thickness tuning alone. The hypothesis draws from recalled thin-film design practice: quarter-wave stacks create high-reflectance bands, and introducing thickness asymmetry or defect layers can open transmission windows. This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone with no literature retrieval.

routes.title: HfO2/MgF2 29-layer UV bandpass with relaxed edge bounds and reduced curvature regularization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with asymmetric thickness tuning can produce a transmission peak in 255-280 nm while maintaining suppression in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands, and broader thickness perturbation ranges will escape the rigid alternating pattern observed in prior rounds.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: alternating high/low index layers create distributed Bragg reflectors; transmission bands appear at wavelengths where the optical thickness condition is violated or at intentional defect layers. MgF2 has low absorption in deep UV; HfO2 provides high index contrast. Breaking quarter-wave symmetry can shift the passband.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | SiO2 substrate (29 film layers total)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers with bounds relaxed to ±2.0 nm from initial quarter-wave values
curvature regularization weight reduced from 0.15 to 0.08
thickness reinitialization with broader uniform perturbation to break alternating pattern
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity of all candidates
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30-layer limit)
HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional e-beam or thermal evaporable dielectrics
individual layer thicknesses should remain in depositable range 30-200 nm
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index ratio nH/nL
Recalled: MgF2 remains transparent down to ~120 nm, suitable for 255-280 nm UV
Recalled: HfO2 has high index (~2.0-2.4 in UV) and low extinction in solar-blind region
Recalled: Breaking periodicity in layer thicknesses can create transmission defects in Bragg mirrors
Recalled: Edge layers have disproportionate effect on impedance matching and passband shape
expected_advantages: Relaxed edge bounds allow larger impedance-matching adjustments at air and substrate interfaces
Reduced curvature regularization permits more aggressive thickness variation between adjacent layers
Broader perturbation ranges should escape local minima from rigid alternating patterns
HfO2/MgF2 pair offers sufficient index contrast for UV bandpass without metal absorption losses
known_risks: I am uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal versus fewer layers; this was chosen to stay under 30-layer limit while maximizing design freedom
I recall HfO2 absorption increases below 250 nm but am uncertain of exact extinction coefficient at 255 nm; measured dataset will resolve this
The exact quarter-wave thickness at 265 nm (center of passband) depends on refractive indices I have not looked up; initial guesses may be off by 10-20%
Curvature regularization weight reduction from 0.15 to 0.08 is a heuristic choice; optimal value is unknown without literature
I am uncertain whether MgF2 stress or adhesion issues would affect 29-layer deposition; this route assumes ideal layers
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer planar multilayer thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2 (29 film layers). Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses simultaneously. Initial thicknesses: quarter-wave at 265 nm center wavelength using measured n values from hfo2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) datasets. Thickness bounds: ±2.0 nm relaxation from initial quarter-wave values for edge layers (layers 1, 2, 28, 29), ±1.5 nm for interior layers. Curvature regularization weight: 0.08. Reinitialize thickness parameters with uniform perturbation range ±5 nm to break alternating patterns. Spectral targets: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Use gradient_thickness optimizer. Total layers fixed at 29.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control route with relaxed edge layer bounds (±1.0 nm to ±2.0 nm), reduced curvature regularization (0.15 to 0.08), and broader thickness perturbation ranges to escape rigid alternating pattern observed in prior rounds per feedback directives.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
